description: Stage-specific combatant configuration used by Story, Arcade and PvE battle modes: character/variant selection, starting status, AI behaviour and per-instance row/rate overrides.

Id.technical: FName import key/row name for FGameDataTableRow_MissionCharacter. Rows are found by this id from wave ally/enemy id lists or from CharacterArcade->Id_MissionCharacter. Besides the row identity, the only observed direct member read is a diagnostic battle-entry log; gameplay consumers use Id_Character instead.

Id_Character.technical: FName, default None. Copied into Entry.Slot.CharacterId by BattleStory_FillFromMissionCharacter and the Arcade/PvE entry builders, then used to find the FGameDataTableRow_Character in CharacterDataTables (DTM+0x3E0). UI code also uses it to find character image rows and build unique character id lists. A missing row is generally not guarded in these gameplay paths.

VariationIndex.technical: int32, default 0. Copied into Slot.VariationIndex and Setup.VariationIndex; AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows uses it as an unchecked index into Character.Id_CharacterVariation to resolve the variation row. It is also used for capture/voice selection and forwarded into battle entry requests. Exported values include -1, so validity depends on the caller and data.

PoseIndex.technical: int32, default 0. BattleSituationOverview assigns it to Enemies[Index].SituationOverviewPoseIndex; capture code then indexes SituationOverview.Id_SituationOverviewPose[PoseIndex] (recorded as unchecked in the reconstructed source) to pick a FGameDataTableRow_SituationOverviewPose.

MaterialPattern.simple: Initial material pattern for the combatant.
MaterialPattern.technical: int32, default 0. Copied into Slot.MaterialPattern in every mode's battle entry builder; battle base later calls Character.MaterialController->SetMaterialPattern(Entry.Slot.MaterialPattern, nullptr). It is also forwarded in character-select parameters and capture setup.

bDamageMaterialEnabled.simple: Enables the damage/decal material path for this combatant.
bDamageMaterialEnabled.technical: bool, default false. Copied into Setup.StatusSetup-adjacent Byte9C in all battle modes; AGameCharacter::ApplyCharacterSetup tests Setup.Byte9C == 1 and calls MaterialController->ResetDecalWeight(). The reconstructed name describes the data flag; the concrete observed effect is the reset call.

bSpecialTagComboSoloEnabled.simple: Allows duplicate hit records in solo special-tag combos.
bSpecialTagComboSoloEnabled.technical: bool, default false. Copied into Setup.Byte9D, then to AGameCharacter::bSetupSpecialTagComboSoloEnabled. The interface accessor AllowsDuplicateHitRecord returns this byte, which is read by hit-record processing; it is therefore not merely serialized.

HitPoint.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Setup.StatusSetup.HitPointOverride. UGameCharacterStatusController::ApplyHitPointParameters uses it only when > 0; otherwise the base-parameter row supplies HitPoint/HitPoint_Solo. GamePvE_CalcMissionCharacterHitPoint also reads it directly, falls back to the base row when <= 0, then adds equipment/binding-vow bonuses and clamps the result to at least 1.0.

Cost.simple: Stock/deployment cost charged when this combatant loses stock.
Cost.technical: int32, default 0. Copied to StatusSetup.Int44 and stored as UGameCharacterStatusController::MissionCharacterCost. Battle systems add it to TeamSpent/CostByTeam, and KO/stock functions call GetStockAfterLoss(MissionCharacterCost). In PvE enemy setup the row value is the base Cost before binding-vow Cost bonuses are added and the result is cast back to int32.

CursedEnergyLevel.technical: int32, default 0. Copied to Setup.Int8C and then AGameCharacter::SetupCursedEnergyLevel. AGameCharacterManager::ApplyCharactersStartStatus calls SetCursedEnergyToLevel when it is > 0; binding vows that force a full level can replace it with Setup.StatusSetup.Int40 + 1 and disable round reset.

bResetCursedEnergyLevelEnabled.simple: Whether cursed energy returns to its initial level on round reset.
bResetCursedEnergyLevelEnabled.technical: bool, default false. Copied to StatusSetup.Byte4C and then UGameCharacterStatusController::bResetCursedEnergyLevelOnRoundReset, which is consulted during round reset; forcing-vow paths can turn the flag off.

TensionLevel.technical: int32, default 0. Copied to Setup.Int90 and then SetupTensionLevel. At battle start, values > 0 become SetTensionGauge((level - 1) * 100.0f), so exported 0 leaves the controller's initial gauge untouched.

PassionGauge.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Setup.Float94 and then SetupPassionGauge; at battle start a value > 0 is passed to SetPassionGaugeValue. Exported rows are all 0.0, which leaves the controller default.

UniqueMode.technical: int32, default 0. Copied to Setup.Int98 and stored as AGameCharacter::SetupUniqueMode. Many character action controllers branch on this value (for example CP_051 selects different passive buffs), so it changes behaviour rather than only display.

CharacterSpecialTagComboLimit.technical: EGameCharacterSpecialTagComboLimit, default None. Cast to uint8 into Setup.Byte89, stored as AGameCharacter::SetupSpecialTagComboLimit, exposed by GetCharacterSpecialTagComboLimit and compared by battle-state logic (for example Performers[0].SetupSpecialTagComboLimit != 2). Exported values are None, Both and Unique; the exact enum-to-effect mapping is not further decoded by these consumers.

Id_CharacterBaseParameter.simple: Override for the character base-parameter row.
Id_CharacterBaseParameter.technical: FName, default None. GameMissionCharacter_CopyOverrideIds copies it into Setup.Overrides.BaseParameterIdOverride; GameCharacter_Override prefers a non-None override, otherwise the base Character row's Id_CharacterBaseParameter is used to resolve CharacterBaseParameterDataTables. GamePvE_CalcMissionCharacterHitPoint independently starts from this field and falls back to Character.Id_CharacterBaseParameter when None.

Id_CharacterCursedEnergy.simple: Override for the cursed-energy parameter row.
Id_CharacterCursedEnergy.technical: FName, default None. Copied into Setup.Overrides.CursedEnergyIdOverride; AGameCharacter::ResolveDataRows uses the non-None value instead of Character.Id_CharacterCursedEnergy when resolving CharacterCursedEnergyDataTables (DTM+0x410).

Id_CharacterSpecialAttack.simple: Override for the character special-attack row.
Id_CharacterSpecialAttack.technical: FName, default None. Copied into Setup.Overrides.SpecialAttackIdOverride; ResolveDataRows uses it instead of Character.Id_CharacterSpecialAttack when finding the CharacterSpecialAttack row (DTM+0x420). A resolved special attack row also leads to its domain-expansion/map data in preload. None means the base character row wins.

Id_CharacterAnimationSet.simple: Override for the character animation-set row.
Id_CharacterAnimationSet.technical: FName, default None. Copied into Setup.Overrides.AnimationSetIdOverride. BattleBase chooses the override when non-None and uses it to preload CharacterAnimationSet montage assets; exported rows with None fall back to Character.Id_CharacterAnimationSet.

Id_CharacterSound.simple: Override for the character sound row.
Id_CharacterSound.technical: FName, default None. Copied into Setup.Overrides.SoundIdOverride. ResolveDataRows first tries this override; only when it is None does it use the Variation row's Id_CharacterSound (DTM+0x510) to resolve CharacterSoundDataTables. Thus a non-None stage value replaces the variation's sound set.

Id_Action.simple: Override for the main action row.
Id_Action.technical: FName, default None. Copied into Setup.Overrides.ActionIdOverride; ResolveDataRows uses it instead of Character.Id_Action for ActionDataTables (DTM+0x5B0). The resolved Action row then supplies Id_ActionMove, Id_ActionJump, Id_ActionBreakFall and the defaults for dash/step.

Id_ActionDash.simple: Override for the dash action row.
Id_ActionDash.technical: FName, default None. Copied into Setup.Overrides.ActionDashIdOverride; ResolveDataRows resolves ActionDashDataTables (DTM+0x5E0) from this value when non-None, otherwise from the resolved Action row's Id_ActionDash. Exported rows use None, so the Action row normally supplies it.

Id_ActionStep.simple: Override for the step action row.
Id_ActionStep.technical: FName, default None. Copied into Setup.Overrides.ActionStepIdOverride; ResolveDataRows resolves ActionStepDataTables (DTM+0x5F0) from this value when non-None, otherwise from the resolved Action row's Id_ActionStep. Exported rows use None.

Damage_Rate.simple: Per-instance multiplier for sent attack damage.
Damage_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f in the row struct; the FGameCharacterRates destination defaults to 1.0f. GameMissionCharacter_CopyOverrideRates copies it to Setup.Overrides.Rates.Scale48, which is copied to AGameCharacter+0x378 and multiplied into the team x action x status damage rate in GAISlot141.

AutoCombo_Damage_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale4C; AGameCharacter::GetAutoComboDamageRate returns CharacterRow->DamageRate_AutoCombo * Rates.Scale4C.

Armor_Damage_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale50; AGameCharacter::GetArmorDamageRate returns that rate directly to damage processing.

Down_Damage_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale54; the character interface accessor GetDownDamageRateScale returns it for damage handling.

GuardDurability_Damage_Rate.simple: Per-instance multiplier for guard-durability damage sent.
GuardDurability_Damage_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale58. GetSendGuardDurabilityDamageRate multiplies team ally rate x status rate x Scale58.

Destructible_Attack_Rate.simple: Per-instance multiplier for attacks on destructible objects.
Destructible_Attack_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale5C; AGameCharacter::GetDestructibleAttackRate returns that value.

CursedEnergyExp_Add_Attacker_Rate.simple: Per-instance cursed-energy experience gain multiplier for the attacker.
CursedEnergyExp_Add_Attacker_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale60. GetCursedEnergyExpRate multiplies status rate x Scale60 x team/stock/level/buff factors, but returns 1.0f when the receiver is null.

CursedEnergyExp_Add_Receiver_Rate.simple: Per-instance cursed-energy experience multiplier when receiving an attack.
CursedEnergyExp_Add_Receiver_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale64; AGameCharacter::GetCursedEnergyExpAddReceiverRate exposes it to the damage/receiver calculation.

TensionGauge_Add_Attacker_Rate.simple: Per-instance tension-gain multiplier for the attacker.
TensionGauge_Add_Attacker_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale68; GetDealtTensionGaugeGainRate returns it (both damage-row and receiver parameters are unused in the reconstructed body).

PassionGauge_Add_Attacker_Rate.simple: Per-instance passion-gain multiplier for the attacker.
PassionGauge_Add_Attacker_Rate.technical: float, default 0.0f. Copied to Rates.Scale6C; GetPassionGaugeAddAttackerRate returns it directly.

Operation.technical: EGameCharacterOperation, default None. Cast to uint8 into Setup.ByteA4 and passed as the AIType argument to AGameCharacter::CreateBrain. When ByteA4 is 0xFF the brain falls back to CharacterRow->AIType, so the row's operation value selects the AI operation when not None/0xFF. Exported values include Invalid, Carefully, Berserker and Onslaught.

AILevel.simple: AI difficulty/level value for the brain.
AILevel.technical: int32, default 0. Copied into Setup.IntA0 and passed as Value174 to CreateBrain/BrainSet174_94; a value of -1 is converted to 10 there. Exported rows use -1, 1, 2 and 4.

notes: The exported asset has 701 rows and uses FGameDataTableRow_MissionCharacter; the manager loads MissionCharacterDataTable into MissionCharacterDataTables (DTM+0x9C0). No numbered shards or localization variants of this table were supplied.

The same row struct is shared by Story, Arcade and PvE entry builders; the reconstructed fill functions copy the row into FStudioBattleCharacterEntry rather than keeping the data table pointer as the only state. Aliases to follow are Setup.StatusSetup.*, Setup.Overrides.*, Setup.Overrides.Rates.*, Slot.* and AGameCharacter::Rates.

The ten rate fields are copied wholesale by GameMissionCharacter_CopyOverrideRates (retail 0x126e320) and then copied to AGameCharacter+0x378. Individual accessor names are reconstructed; the status scoreboard should be consulted before treating them as byte-matched retail names.

Finders such as 0x12fae20 and 0x12fb1e0 are labelled behavioural in status/functions.json. Several consumers index arrays without bounds checks as recorded; documentation describes that behaviour rather than promising safety.
Only reconstructed C++ and the supplied export were reviewed; Content is partial, so this is not a claim about every retail or Blueprint use.

usages.detail: BattleStory_FillFromMissionCharacter copies nearly all row fields into a battle character entry.
GameMissionCharacter_CopyOverrideIds copies the eight row-id overrides.
GameMissionCharacter_CopyOverrideRates copies the ten rate multipliers.
ResolveDataRows consumes the id overrides and VariationIndex to resolve the base character's related rows.
ApplyCharacterSetup copies rates and scalar setup values into the live AGameCharacter.
Status initialization consumes HitPoint and Cost-derived fields and the cursed-energy reset flag.
ApplyCharactersStartStatus turns initial cursed-energy/tension/passion values into live gauge state.
Arcade enemy entries copy the same fields from mission-character rows found through wave ids.
Uses enemy mission-character rows to assign situation-overview pose indices.
